runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — Joe's program as it stands, and the change in progress**

**Where things stand**

Joe moved onto this engine on 1 Nov 2026 with a fresh program. The version in force is the third one, an amendment adopted on 4 Nov 2026, with a hypertrophy emphasis. The reason recorded for it: the latest engine release lifted three cutover workarounds — counted pull-up variants now give the pull-up a real weekly dose target, and a conditioning session can sit beside a lifting day, so the kettlebell swing finisher left the Monday session and became its own every-minute-on-the-minute session.

No warnings were raised by any of the reads we ran. The progress report is empty on dose so far — no weekly set targets and no completed weeks to compare against — which is expected this early; it fills in once the current block has weeks behind it.

**The week (six days, Thursday off)**

Tuesday is the personal trainer at the gym, which Joe does not control. It alternates chest and back (planned as roughly 6 chest, 6 lat and 3 biceps sets) with legs and core (roughly 6 quad, 4 glute and 4 abdominal sets). Weekday home sessions are capped at about 75 minutes, weekends at about 90.

*Monday — OHP, back and arms (75 min)*
- Overhead Press (Barbell): warm-ups of 1×5 and 1×3, then a top set of 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 back-off sets.
- Chest Supported Row (Dumbbell): 4×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8.
- Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8.

*Wednesday — Pull-up volume and core (75 min, lift in the morning before the lunchtime run)*
- Scapular Pull Up: 2 activation sets of 6–8 at RPE 5.
- Negative Pull Up: 3×2–4 at RPE 8.
- Pull Up (Band): 4×5–8 at RPE 8.
- Flexed Arm Hang: 2 holds of 20 seconds.
- Lying Leg Raise: 3×10–15 at RPE 8.
- Suitcase Carry: 4 carries of 30 seconds.
- Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8.

*Friday — Strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75 min)*
- Pull Up: one all-out test single (1×1 at RPE 10).
- Back Squat (Barbell): warm-ups of 1×5, 1×3 and 1×2, a top set of 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×5 back-off.
- Romanian Deadlift (Barbell): 3×6–10 at RPE 8.
- Split Squat (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Shoulder Press (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8.
- Ab Wheel Rollout: 3×6–12 at RPE 8.

*Saturday — Bench, back and arms (90 min)*
- Bench Press (Barbell): warm-ups of 1×8, 1×5 and 1×3, a top set of 1×5 at RPE 8, then 4×6 back-off.
- Bent Over Row (Barbell): 4×6–10 at RPE 8.
- Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Dip Negatives: 3×3–5 at RPE 8.
- Overhead Triceps Extension (Dumbbell): 3×10–15 at RPE 8.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell): 3×12–15 at RPE 8.

*Sunday — Deadlift and legs (90 min)*
- Deadlift (Barbell): warm-ups of 1×5 and 1×3, a top set of 1×5 at RPE 8, then 3×5 back-off.
- Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Hip Thrust (Barbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Pull Up (Band): 3×5–8 at RPE 8.
- Bicep Curl (Dumbbell): 3×8–12 at RPE 8.
- Hammer Curl (Dumbbell): 3×10–12 at RPE 8.
- Farmers Walk (Dumbbell): 3 carries of 30 seconds.

*Optional sessions*
- Kettlebell swing EMOM (weekly): 12 swings every minute for 12 minutes at RPE 7. It grows by 2 minutes at a time up to 16 minutes, and reps can rise to 15 per minute.
- Strength circuit (standing, any week): 4 rounds of Goblet Squat ×10, Ring Push Up ×12, Kettlebell Swing ×12, Mountain Climber ×16 at RPE 8, within a 16-minute cap; rounds can climb to 6.
- Daily dead hang: 2 holds of 20 seconds at RPE 5.

How the big lifts progress: the barbell top set is the driver and the back-off sets follow it. Everything else is double progression — hold the load until every set hits the top of the rep range, then add weight. Pull-ups and dips build through negatives first and banded volume second, progressing by shrinking the band rather than chasing reps; strict sets become real work once the test single passes about five. One standing rule to keep in view: the home bar tops out at 228 lb, so when a squat or deadlift top set reaches about 220 lb, that lift moves to the gym.

**What we noticed, and the change in progress**

Comparing this program to the one Joe ran before 1 Nov: the old plan had Incline Curl (Dumbbell) in both of its pull sessions, alongside Bicep Curl and Hammer Curl. The new program's only direct biceps work is Sunday — Bicep Curl 3×8–12 and Hammer Curl 3×10–12 — plus whatever the trainer gives on Tuesday (about 3 sets). Monday, titled "OHP, back and arms", currently has no arm isolation at all beyond the row's indirect biceps work.

The proposal: add Incline Curl (Dumbbell) as the fifth and final exercise on Monday, 3×8–12 at RPE 8, progressing by double progression like the other dumbbell lines. This fits Joe's stated preference that direct biceps work is dumbbell curls, not barbell.

Nothing has been written yet — the change has been opened but not adopted. If it goes through, it would record a fourth program version as an amendment, with Monday growing from four exercises to five and the rest of the week untouched. It would not change anything in Hevy until the next week's plan is pushed.

What Joe needs to agree to before it is adopted:
1. Adding roughly 3 hard biceps sets to Monday, so his weekly direct biceps volume rises from about 6 home sets (plus the trainer's ~3) to about 9 (plus ~3).
2. Monday getting a few minutes longer — it has to stay inside the 75-minute weekday cap, so if it runs over, something else on Monday gives, not the cap.
3. A starting load per hand for the incline curl. None is set yet; he should pick a weight he can hit 8 clean reps with at RPE 8 on the first set, and the engine will take it from there.

If he says yes to all three, the amendment can be adopted and Monday will carry the new line from the next planned week.

first.text:
Here's what changes, and one thing I need from you before I lock it in.

**Monday becomes five exercises.** Incline Curl (Dumbbell) goes in last, after the rear delt flys: 3 sets of 8 to 12 at RPE 8. Same progression rule as your other dumbbell work: hold the weight until every set reaches 12 clean reps, then go up. Nothing else in the week moves. Sunday keeps its bicep curls and hammer curls, so direct biceps work goes from 6 sets a week to 9, spread over two days, plus whatever your trainer gives you on Tuesday.

**Time.** Monday has room for it inside the 75 minutes. If it ever runs long, the curls are the first thing to drop that day, not the OHP or the rows.

**Starting weight.** I need a number per hand. Pick a dumbbell you're confident you can curl for 8 strict reps on an incline with two or three reps left in the tank. If you're unsure, go lighter than you think: the incline position is harder than a standing curl, so your usual curl weight is probably too heavy. For reference, your Sunday bicep curl weight minus one or two dumbbell steps is a reasonable guess.

Give me the weight and a yes, and Monday carries the curls from next week's plan. Nothing in Hevy changes until that plan goes out.
